validation.projectKey: Use {min} to {max} lowercase letters, digits and single hyphens, starting with a letter.

validation.connectorUrl: Enter an address starting with http:// or https://.
validation.outputKey: Use letters, digits and underscores only.
validation.secretName: Use capital letters, digits and underscores, starting with a letter (at most 64).
validation.headerName: Use letters, digits and hyphens only.
validation.wholeNumberMax: Enter a whole number up to {max}, or leave it empty.
validation.fieldPath: Use field names joined by dots, e.g. decision or result.band.
validation.fieldPathLines: Write one field per line, as names joined by dots, e.g. applicant.nationalId.
validation.fieldPathSegments: Use names of letters, digits and underscores joined by dots, e.g. applicant.age.
validation.fieldPathTaken: Another field already has this name.

signIn.title: Sign in
signIn.description: Sign in to Donka Studio with your work email.

forgotPassword.title: Reset your password
forgotPassword.description: Enter your work email. If it has an account, we send a link to choose a new password.
forgotPassword.sent: If {email} has an account, a link is on its way. It works once and expires soon.

setupPassword.title: Choose your password
setupPassword.description: Use at least {min} characters. A long phrase is easier to remember and harder to guess.
setupPassword.missingToken: This page needs the link from your email. Open the link again, or ask for a new one.
setupPassword.done: Sign in with your email and new password.

session.errorTitle: We could not check your session

notFound.title: Page not found
notFound.description: This page does not exist or has moved.

projects.title: Projects
projects.emptyAdmin: Create the first project to start building decisions.
projects.emptyMember: You are not a member of any project yet. Ask a project owner to add you.
projects.emptyArchived: Projects you archive appear here and can be restored.
projects.errorTitle: We could not load your projects
projects.createDescription: You become the project's owner and can add members afterwards.
projects.name: Name
projects.keyHint: Used in links and release paths. It cannot change later.
projects.descriptionHint: Optional. What decisions this project holds.

project.archivedNotice: This project is archived: it is read-only until an owner restores it.
project.detailsDescription: The key cannot change: releases and links depend on it.
project.readOnlyDetails: Only owners can change these details.
project.archivedDetails: Restore the project to change these details.
project.archiveDescription: Archived projects are read-only and hidden from the project list. You can restore them.
project.archiveConfirm: Nobody can change it until an owner restores it. Nothing is deleted.
project.restoreDescription: Make the project editable again and show it in the project list.

members.title: Members
members.removeConfirm: They lose access to {project} at once. You can add them again later.
members.addDescription: The person needs a Studio account. An administrator invites new people.
members.errorTitle: We could not load the members
members.inviteAndAdd: Invite {email} to Studio and add them
members.invitedAndAdded: {email} was invited to Studio and added. They receive an email to choose their password.
members.noAccountAdmin: No Studio account uses {email} yet. You can invite them and add them to the project in one step.
members.empty: Add the people who work on this project.

people.title: People
people.description: Everyone with a Studio account. Invite people here, then add them to projects.
people.inviteDescription: They receive an email to choose their password. The link works once and expires.
people.isAdminHint: Administrators create projects and invite people.
people.invited: An invitation is on its way to {email}.
people.resent: A new invitation is on its way to {email}. The previous link no longer works.
people.errorTitle: We could not load the accounts
people.empty: Invite the people who build and approve decisions.

audit.title: Audit log
audit.ownersOnly: Only the project's owners can see its audit log.
audit.emptyRange: The end date is before the start date.
audit.errorTitle: We could not load the audit log
audit.empty: Nothing has been recorded for this project yet.

auditSentences.memberRoleChanged: Changed the role of {person} from {from} to {to}
auditSentences.approvalRequested: Asked for release {version} to go to production
auditSentences.approvalWithdrawn: Withdrew the production request for release {version}
auditSentences.decisionLogPurged: Purged {records} decision records older than {days} days
auditSentences.decisionLogResealed: Re-sealed {records} decision records with the current key
auditSentences.decisionLogSettingsUpdated: Set the decision log's outcome field to {field}
auditSentences.decisionLogSettingsCleared: Removed the decision log's outcome field
auditSentences.decisionRecordExplained: Asked for an explanation of the {key} decision {reference}

command.title: Command menu
command.description: Open a page or project, or change a preference.

decisions.title: Decisions
decisions.createDescription: It opens empty in the editor. Other decisions call it by its key.
decisions.keyHint: For example person-score, or bureau/normalize to keep it in a folder.
decisions.keyTaken: Another decision in this project already uses this key.
decisions.empty: Create the first decision of this project, then build it in the editor.
decisions.emptyReadOnly: Editors and owners of this project create its decisions.
decisions.errorTitle: We could not load the decisions
decisions.deleteConfirm: Its draft is deleted. Decisions that call it will fail until they call another one.
decisions.notFound: This project has no decision named {key}. It may have been deleted or renamed.
decisions.conflictBy: {email} saved it <when></when> while you were editing. Load their version, or keep yours and replace theirs.
decisions.conflict: It was saved while you were editing. Load the saved version, or keep yours and replace it.
decisions.nodeDescription: Call another decision of the project

versions.saveDescription: Keeps the draft as it is now. Versions never change; you can compare or restore them later.
versions.messageHint: A short note for reviewers, e.g. “Raise the income threshold to 150,000”.
versions.unchanged: Nothing changed since the last version
versions.empty: Save a version to keep the draft as it is now.
versions.emptyReadOnly: An editor has not saved a version yet.
versions.compareDescription: The newer side, with what changed from the older side.
versions.restoreConfirm: Its content replaces the draft and is saved as version {number}. Draft changes that were not saved as a version are lost.

scenarios.title: Test scenarios
scenarios.dialogDescription: An input to a decision and the output it should give. Every version saved runs all of the project's scenarios.
scenarios.name: Name
scenarios.nameTaken: Another scenario of this decision has this name.
scenarios.partialHint: Passes when every expected field has its value; other fields of the output are free.
scenarios.exactHint: Passes only when the output is exactly the expected JSON.
scenarios.errorTitle: The scenarios could not be loaded
scenarios.empty: Write what a decision should answer for a given input; every version saved will check it.
scenarios.emptyReadOnly: An editor has not written a scenario yet.
scenarios.emptyNoDecision: Create a decision first, then write what it should answer.
scenarios.deleteConfirm: Versions already tested keep their results. New versions will not run it.

tests.title: Tests on version {number}
tests.description: How every scenario of the project went when this version was saved.
tests.none: No scenario ran on this version.
tests.noVersion: Could not run: {key} has no saved version yet.

releases.title: Releases
releases.createDescription: A release freezes the latest saved version of every decision. It never changes afterwards.
releases.notesHint: What changed and why, for the people who deploy and audit it.
releases.deployConfirm: The Runtime serving staging switches to this release within a minute.
releases.empty: Save a version of each decision, then create a release to deploy it.
releases.unversioned: A release only contains saved versions. Save a version of these decisions first:
releases.nothing: This project has no decisions yet.
releases.failing: You can still release; the results are kept with the release.

environments.title: Environments
environments.stagingDescription: Where a release is tried before production.
environments.productionDescription: What your systems call for real decisions.
environments.productionApproval: Production is published after an owner who neither made the release nor asked for it approves it.
environments.noRelease: Create a release to deploy it here.
environments.requestConfirm: The project’s owners are emailed. One of them reviews what changes and the test results, then approves or rejects it.

tokens.title: Runtime tokens
tokens.createDescription: Your systems send it to the Runtime to call this project’s decisions.
tokens.name: Name
tokens.nameHint: Who or what uses it, to find it later.
tokens.shownOnce: Copy it now: it is shown only once. Studio keeps only a fingerprint.
tokens.header: Send it in the X-Access-Token header. It works within a minute.
tokens.empty: No tokens. Create one for each system that calls the Runtime.
tokens.revokeConfirm: Calls with this token are refused within a minute. This cannot be undone.

approvals.title: Approvals
approvals.errorTitle: Approval requests could not be loaded
approvals.empty: Production requests appear here. Ask for one from the Environments page once a release is live on staging.
approvals.authorCannotDecide: You made this release or asked for it: another owner decides.
approvals.waitingForOwner: Waiting for an owner of the project to decide.
approvals.noTests: This project has no test scenarios.
approvals.failingTests: Some scenarios fail on this release. Check they are expected before approving.
approvals.approvedTitle: Approved by {email}: the release is on its way to production.
approvals.changesSummary: {count, plural, one {# decision changes} other {# decisions change}} compared with production.
approvals.firstProduction: Nothing is in production yet: every decision is new.
approvals.approveConfirm: It is published to production within a minute. Systems calling the production Runtime get its decisions.
approvals.rejectDescription: Say why, so the team knows what to change. Production stays as it is.
approvals.reasonHint: Shown on the request and kept in the audit log.
approvals.withdrawConfirm: Owners can no longer approve it. You can ask again later.
approvals.contractBreaking: Input fields: {count, plural, one {# breaking change} other {# breaking changes}}

contractKinds.presentation: label, help or personal-data mark changed

rollback.title: Roll production back
rollback.description: Put a release approved for production before back live. No new approval is needed; the audit log records it.
rollback.releaseHint: Releases approved for production, except the one live now.
rollback.reasonHint: What went wrong, for the team and the audit log.

connector.nodeDescription: Call a bureau, KYC or AML service
connector.title: Connector settings
connector.presetHint: Choosing a template fills in its settings; the address stays.
connector.urlHint: The Runtime sends the request body here as JSON (POST). Studio never calls it.
connector.secretHint: Only the name is stored. The Runtime reads the value from {variable}.
connector.bodyHint: JSON. Text values may use the decision's input, e.g. {example}.
connector.outputKeyHint: The service's answer is added to the decision's data under this name.
connector.reliability: When the service is slow or fails
connector.timeoutHint: Per attempt. Empty: the Runtime's default.
connector.retriesHint: After a server error or timeout. Empty: the Runtime's default.

onErrorOption.fail: Stop the decision with an error

connector.fallbackHint: JSON used as the answer when the service fails.
connector.mockHint: JSON the simulator and test scenarios use as the service's answer.

decisionLog.title: Decision log
decisionLog.emptyRange: The last day comes before the first: no decision can match.
decisionLog.errorTitle: The decision log could not be loaded.
decisionLog.empty: Decisions appear here once a Runtime serving this project sends them. An administrator issues a decision-log token under Runtimes and sets it on the Runtime.
decisionLog.emptyFiltered: Try other filters, or clear them.
decisionLog.recordOf: Decision {key}, as the Runtime made it.
decisionLog.viewAudited: This record holds an applicant's personal data. Opening and replaying it are recorded in the project's audit log.
decisionLog.traceDescription: What each node of the decision received and returned.
decisionLog.identical: Release {version} gives the same answer again.
decisionLog.different: Release {version} now gives another answer than the one recorded.
decisionLog.settingsDescription: Each decision a Runtime makes is recorded. The outcome field is read from its answer when it arrives, so the log can be searched by outcome; the redacted fields never leave Studio when a decision is explained.
decisionLog.outcomeFieldHint: A field of the decision's output, e.g. decision or result.band. Leave empty for none; failed decisions are always error.
decisionLog.explanationNote: Written by {model} from this record, without the project's redacted fields. It explains; it changes nothing.
decisionLog.redactedFields: Fields never sent for an explanation
decisionLog.redactedFieldsHint: One field per line, e.g. applicant.nationalId. They are removed from what the decision read and answered, and from its trace, before a record is sent to be explained. At most {max}.
decisionLog.redactedFieldsHintOff: One field per line, e.g. applicant.nationalId. Explanations are off in this installation; the list applies once they are on. At most {max}.
decisionLog.viewAuditedExplain: This record holds an applicant's personal data. Opening, replaying and explaining it are recorded in the project's audit log.

runtimes.title: Runtimes
runtimes.description: Each Runtime sends the decisions it makes to Studio's decision log with a token issued here for its environment.
runtimes.name: Name
runtimes.empty: Issue a token for each environment, then set it on its Runtimes so their decisions reach the decision log.
runtimes.revokeConfirm: Runtimes using it can no longer send decisions; those they still hold are dropped. This cannot be undone.
runtimes.createDescription: A token lets the Runtimes of one environment send their decisions to Studio.
runtimes.shownOnce: Copy the token now: Studio keeps only its hash and will not show it again.
runtimes.nameHint: Who uses it, e.g. the Runtime's host.
runtimes.oneEnvironment: This token only sends {environment} decisions: records from another environment are refused.

ciTokens.title: CI tokens
ciTokens.description: Pipelines pull this project's releases with these tokens. Targets: main (the newest release), release:1.4.0, commit:RELEASE_ID, env:staging or env:production. A token only reads this project.
ciTokens.createDescription: A pipeline sends it to download this project's release artifacts. It cannot change anything.
ciTokens.name: Name
ciTokens.nameHint: Which pipeline uses it, to find it later.
ciTokens.shownOnce: Copy it now: it is shown only once. Studio keeps only a fingerprint.
ciTokens.targets: The pipeline posts to /api/v1/rules-sync with the token as a bearer and downloads the artifact it is given.
ciTokens.empty: No CI tokens. Create one for each pipeline that pulls this project's releases.
ciTokens.emptyReadOnly: No CI tokens. Owners create them.
ciTokens.revokeConfirm: Pipelines using it are refused at once. This cannot be undone.

inputFields.title: Input fields
inputFields.description: What a request to this decision must contain. The Runtime refuses a request that breaks these rules, naming the field; forms are built from the same definition.
inputFields.emptyDescription: Requests are not checked. Add the fields this decision reads to check them and to tell form builders what to send.
inputFields.dialogDescription: Its name, type and rules are checked on every request; labels and help are for forms.
inputFields.label: Label
inputFields.piiLong: Personal data (never sent to be explained)
inputFields.pathHint: Field names joined by dots, as rules read it, e.g. applicant.age.
inputFields.valuesHint: Comma-separated; leave empty to accept any value.
inputFields.jsonHint: For what the table cannot express, such as lists or patterns. Labels and help go under "x-donka".
inputFields.jsonOnly: This schema uses rules the table cannot show (lists, patterns or combinations). Edit it in the JSON Schema tab.
inputFields.unreadable: The schema on the Request node is not valid JSON. Fix it in the JSON Schema tab: until then, requests are not checked and the version cannot be saved.
inputFields.noInputNode: Add a Request node to the graph first: the input fields are kept on it.
inputFields.undeclared: {path} is read by the rules but is not an input field: requests may not carry it.
inputFields.unread: {path} is required but no rule reads it: callers send it for nothing.
